title: No tested simple template constraint forces more than nested behavior

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No tested simple template constraint forces more than nested behavior

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Of the 137,438,953,472 template constraints with a required-template condition, none of the millions tested forces anything more complicated than nested behavior.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: of the millions of these that I have tested, none have forced anything more complicated than the kind of nested behavior seen on the previous page.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Systems Based on Constraints” (from p. 210), p. 220. Scope: two-dimensional template constraints with a required-template condition

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A new public enumeration can test a defined sample, but the historical tested set and complexity criterion are not fully recoverable from the claim. No feasible sample establishes the whole finite population.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Specify a reproducible sample of required-template constraints and a quantitative hierarchy separating nested from more complex patterns, then search for forced satisfying configurations. A verified system above the nested category refutes the empirical generalization.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The tested fraction of 137 billion systems is small and possibly biased.

“More complicated than nested” is underspecified.

The original millions tested are not supplied as a reusable dataset.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.22
analysis feasibility: 0.38
operationalizability: 0.5
data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is carefully limited to millions tested, so it is a sample claim rather than a universal theorem, but that sample is not deposited as data. A new sample of millions is a proxy, and millions remain a thin slice of 137,438,953,472 constraints. Finding a clearly non-nested coloring would refute the intended content; failing to find one would not close it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Draw a large explicit sample of required-template constraints, search each for a satisfying coloring, and classify that coloring as repetitive, nested, or neither by a stated substitution or automata test. One coloring that fails both repetitive and nested tests would refute the sample claim; a clean sample only supports it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The millions actually tested are not archived as a list.

A negative search leaves the other constraints in the 137 billion untouched.

Nested versus more complicated is a judgment unless a formal class such as automatic sequences is fixed in advance.

analysis feasibility: 0.4
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.4
